To maximize the total reward in a bandit problem, we must balance exploration (trying unknown arms to gather information) and exploitation (choosing the arm known to provide the highest reward). 

Since "Highest Reward" has already been sampled once and yielded a strong mean of 0.9, while the other two arms have not been sampled at all, it is statistically optimal to explore the other arms to determine if they offer even higher rewards than 0.9.
